proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (fact Gr). The coordinate identities (i)-(ii) of lip_approx_graph_coordinates are re-derived inline, so that this child depends on no other node.

1. By LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul, it suffices to show dist(Gamma x, Gamma z) <= sqrt(2) * dist(x, z) for all x, z in R^n, where Gamma(x) = q(graphPoint x (f x)). The real number underlying NNReal.sqrt 2 is sqrt(2) (Real.coe_sqrt, NNReal.coe_ofNat).

2. Fix x, z. A linear isometry equivalence preserves distances (LinearIsometryEquiv.dist_map), and dist(u, v) = |u - v|. So the claim becomes |D| <= sqrt(2) |x - z|, where D := graphPoint x (f x) - graphPoint z (f z) in R^(n+l).

3. By definition, graphPoint a b = toLp(Fin.append a b).
- Its coordinate at index Fin.castAdd l i (i < n) is a_i, and at index Fin.natAdd n j (j < l) it is b_j (Fin.append_left, Fin.append_right).
- Every index of Fin (n+l) has exactly one of these two forms.
- Subtraction in EuclideanSpace is coordinatewise, so D has coordinate x_i - z_i at castAdd l i and (f x)_j - (f z)_j at natAdd n j.

4. For w in a Euclidean space, |w|^2 = sum_k w_k^2 (EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq). Split the sum over Fin (n+l) into its castAdd and natAdd parts (Fin.sum_univ_add) and use step 3: |D|^2 = sum_{i<n} (x_i - z_i)^2 + sum_{j<l} ((f x)_j - (f z)_j)^2 = |x - z|^2 + |f x - f z|^2.

5. By hypothesis, 0 <= |f x - f z| <= |x - z|. Hence |f x - f z|^2 <= |x - z|^2, and |D|^2 <= 2|x - z|^2 = (sqrt(2) |x - z|)^2, since (sqrt 2)^2 = 2.

6. Both |D| and sqrt(2)|x - z| are nonnegative, and for nonnegative a, b, a^2 <= b^2 implies a <= b (sq_le_sq₀). Hence |D| <= sqrt(2)|x - z|. By steps 1-2, this proves that Gamma is sqrt(2)-Lipschitz.
